cards.subject: The Forest of Elwynn
lines: It was a battlefield in the first Warcraft game, twenty years before it was anybody's starting zone.
Much of it burned in the First War. These trees are the regrowth.

cards.subject: Northshire Abbey
lines: The abbey's first recorded battle is a Warcraft I mission, and the besiegers were not orcs.
"The monks of Northshire Abbey are under siege by a band of warriors that have been convinced by enemy agents to fight against the crown."
The zone where humans learn to fight opened with humans turned against Stormwind.

cards.subject: Goldshire
lines: The name was made up on the fly by one of the designers during the first Warcraft game.
It has stood ever since, and is now probably the most-visited village in any video game.
It and Moonbrook were the last two towns to fall in the First War.

cards.subject: You no take candle
cards.tag: The joke is built into the zone
lines: Kobolds wear candles because they are terrified of the dark. Their own word for dying is that the darkness took them.
The first collection quest most humans ever get sends you into a mine to take exactly those candles.
The most quoted line in Warcraft is a creature begging you not to steal its only light.

cards.subject: Hogger
lines: He was given exactly the number of the beast, the same as the other races' starting-zone bosses.
For most human players he is the first elite tag they ever see, without knowing what it means.
Killing him at level ten was a thing groups organised.

cards.subject: One chain of command
lines: The kobolds in the mines were enslaved by the gnolls.
The gnolls were armed and directed by the Defias.
Everything you kill in your first ten levels reports, eventually, to the same man.

cards.subject: Every bandit is a bricklayer
cards.tag: Why the zone is at war
lines: The guild that rebuilt Stormwind was never paid, and was dissolved when it asked.
The riots that followed killed the Queen, and the Defias came out of them.
The men robbing the roads here built the walls you spawned behind.

cards.subject: Heroes' Vigil
cards.tag: The island in Stone Cairn Lake
lines: A cairn raised for the First War dead. The lake is named after the monument, not the other way round.
It is the Defias who describe it as a bastion of faith now forgotten by Stormwind's own soldiers.
The bandits remember the war dead better than the kingdom does.

cards.subject: Stone Cairn Lake
lines: One island at the centre, which gives it a shape nothing else in the zone has.
It also holds the densest copper in Elwynn, so there are usually miners circling a war memorial.
Murlocs on the south bank, gnolls on the north.

cards.subject: The Tower of Azora
cards.tag: The archmage will not see you
lines: A bolt-hole for mages who wanted out of Stormwind's politics, and its master refuses visitors.
There is an instrument in there for spying on the rival tower across the border in Redridge.
The tower leaks. The living buckets and the odd wildlife in the fields nearby are blamed on it.

cards.subject: Stonefield and Maclure
lines: One family keeps the pumpkins, the other the vineyards, and they have been feuding for years.
Both will send you on errands. Neither mentions the other kindly.
It is the Hatfields and the McCoys, in a starting zone.

cards.subject: Only one wood is safe
lines: The bears, boars and spiders in Northshire will not touch you. The same animals everywhere else in Elwynn will.
It is the only walled valley in the zone and the only one where the wildlife was made harmless on purpose.
Nothing tells you when you cross out of it.

cards.subject: Jerod's Landing
lines: A boat landing on the river in the south-east, held by a Defias dockmaster.
It ran stolen goods down from Redridge into Westfall. Elwynn was the middle of the pipe, not the end of it.
In vanilla it is reached almost entirely through rogue-only quests. Nobody records who Jerod was.
